title: Pocket Slate — response economy playpen
content:
Context / one-liner:
Pocket Slate = a lightweight per-turn response tiering primitive that lets apps opt specific messages into ultra-frugal replies (tiny token budgets, cached slates, short templates) while preserving a clear upgrade path to full-fidelity generation. Goal: save host-token cost on common transactional/assist turns without degrading UX for intentful queries.

Why this?
- We see >40% of application turns being short info/ack flows (confirmations, small facts, formatting). Many of these don't need full LM capacity.
- Hosts want predictable unit economics and easy opt-in controls.
- Existing fallback/caching primitives are heavy to configure per-route. Pocket Slate = simple toggle + conservative defaults.

Key ideas / primitives:
- Slate: a tiny, pre-compiled response template + optional micro-KV prefix (<=512 tokens), quantized offline and stored in slate store.
- Budget envelope: per-slate token budget cap (e.g., 8–48 tokens) + compute tier (micro, standard).
- Probabilistic riser: cheap-first attempt; if confidence low, escalate to higher tier synchronously or async (fast fallback).
- Affinity-based caching: prefetched slates for active sessions or routes.
- Developer API: route-level config: {enabled, budget, fallback_policy, ttl, warm_on_high_traffic}. Default quickstart: enable with budget=24, fallback=sync-upgrade.

User stories (rough):
- As a product engineer, I can mark a route as "pocket-friendly" so transactional messages use the micro-tier automatically.
- As an ops manager, I can see savings and failure rates in Console per-route and set rollout percentage.
- As an end-user, short confirmations should be instant (<200ms) and not truncated; longer queries still get full answers.

Acceptance criteria (MVP):
- Developer API: route flag + two config fields (budget, fallback).
- Runtime: micro-tier model variant available and routable. Pocket slate attempt p50 latency <200ms for cached slates.
- Observability: per-route metrics: pocket_attempts, pocket_success, pocket_escalations, avg_cost_saved.
- Safety: do not return hallucinated facts when escalation not permitted (conservative template sanitization).

Metrics to track:
- % turns routed to pocket tier (goal: 20–50% for trial apps).
- Cost delta tokens/turn and $$ saved vs baseline.
- Escalation rate (attempt->fallback) and user-visible errors.
- Latency p50/p95 of pocket attempts.

Rollout plan (phases):
1) Internal dogfood: single product integration (assistant notifications) - manual config.
2) Beta: expose to selected customers as opt-in. Add per-route rollout % in Console.
3) GA: docs, examples for templates, SDK helpers.

Infra / runtime notes:
- Slate store: small objects, low-IO. Need hot cache (in-memory) for slates used by top 10 routes. Consider redis LRU + local node cache.
- KV prefix TTL: default 10m; resync on session touch.
- Micro-tier model: likely a small quantized variant; need profiling for p50 latency and small-seq perf. Work with model-onboarding to define a compatible candidate.
- Routing: prefer region-local micro-pool; fallback to standard pool via smart routing to preserve SLOs.

Edge cases / open Qs:
- When to escalate? confidence threshold vs deterministic template mismatch.
- How to measure UX impact other than A/B clicks? define synthetic prompts that represent transactional queries.
- Billing implications: do we expose a different price per pocket token vs normal? do we count bytes differently?
- Security: slates may contain templated text that includes PII placeholders. Slate storage must be access-controlled and optionally encrypted.
- Interaction with session-level KV caches: dedupe keys and avoid double-counting.

Prototype plan (next 2 sprints):
- Sprint 1: implement route flag + simple in-memory slate store + micro-tier routing toggle (dev env only). Owner: Mika S.
- Sprint 2: add Console metrics + small beta with Notifications team. Owner: Tess L.
- Spike: quantized micro-model perf and cost sim with 5k synthetic turns. Owner: Ethan C.

Quick implementation notes / sketch:
- API: POST /responses?route=notify&mode=pocket body: { slate_id, user_kv_refs } -> runtime checks slate cache -> run micro model with prefix -> if result.confidence >= X return else escalate.
- Fallback options: sync-upgrade (synchronous call to standard pool), async-backfill (return short ack and generate full answer later), manual (drop).

Notes to self / experiments to run:
- Build 1k templates from top 50 customer routes and simulate pocket success rates.
- Try TTL=60s vs 10m tradeoffs for chatty sessions.
- AB criteria: 5% uplift in perceived responsiveness with <1% increase in overall error rate.

References / inspiration:
- "prefetch-priming-profiles" notes (look up in Drive)
- Related ticket JIRA-IR-1423 (routing policy flags)

Open next-steps (today):
- Draft quickstart sample for Console (Tess)
- Ping model-onboarding for micro-variant candidate (Ethan)
- Add initial experiment tracking to metrics backlog (Mika)

-- end of scratchpad --

(This is intentionally rough — want to capture quick heuristics and questions before formalizing into a short PRD.)
